glosses: Flexible material in a roll with a sticky surface on one or both sides; adhesive tape.

examples.text: Hand me some tape. I need to fix a tear in this paper.
I sealed up the box with clear shipping tape.

glosses: Thin and flat paper, plastic or similar flexible material, usually produced in the form of a roll.

examples.text: We made some decorative flowers out of the tape we bought.

glosses: Finishing tape, stretched across a track to mark the end of a race.

examples.text: Jones broke the tape in 47.77 seconds, a new world record.

glosses: Magnetic or optical recording media in a roll; videotape or audio tape.

examples.text: Did you get that on tape?
So we went around the corner, looked in the garbage, and, boom, there's about 16 of the tapes he didn't like!

glosses: Any video or audio recording, regardless of the method used to produce it.

examples.text: “It was one of the most severe beatings they’ve seen on tape,” an FDNY insider said, recalling the reaction by brass who viewed video of the bloody fisticuffs.

glosses: An unthinking, patterned response triggered by a particular stimulus.

examples.text: Old couples will sometimes play tapes at each other during a fight.

glosses: The series of prices at which a financial instrument trades.

examples.text: Don’t fight the tape.

glosses: The wrapping of the primary puck-handling surface of a hockey stick

examples.text: His pass was right on the tape.

glosses: A strong flexible band rotating on pulleys for directing the sheets in a printing machine.
